title: IRGC Claims New Attacks on US Warships Over Naval Blockade; Ghalibaf Warns of 'Faster, Heavier, More Painful' Response
detail: The Strait of Hormuz crisis continued into September 6 (Sunday) with no sign of de-escalation: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed fresh attacks on US warships enforcing the ongoing American naval blockade of Iran, which has been in place since the collapse of the June 17 ceasefire memorandum on July 8. Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reiterated that any further attacks on Iran would 'meet a faster, heavier and more painful response,' extending the harder rhetorical line he set the day before ('the era of proportionate responses is over'). The renewed multi-day exchange — US strikes on IRGC targets (Sept 1), Iranian retaliation across Jordan, Kuwait, and the UAE (Sept 2-3), and mutual tanker/vessel strikes in the Strait (Sept 5) — keeps a live war-risk premium in oil markets heading into the new week, with commercial shipping through Hormuz still running far below its pre-crisis baseline and the September 16 FOMC meeting now set against a backdrop of both a hawkish August jobs report and an unresolved energy-supply shock.

title: Energy Secretary Wright: Iran Nuclear Deal 'May Not' Happen, Says US May Instead Destroy Tehran's Capabilities
detail: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on ABC News' 'This Week' on September 6 that a nuclear agreement with Iran may not be reachable anytime soon, seven months into the war that began February 28. 'There may not be a nuclear agreement,' Wright said, adding the alternative path could be 'simply destroying their capabilities to do it' rather than negotiating a deal. He said any formal agreement 'may await the next administration in Iran,' while acknowledging 'we simply don't know that,' and claimed continued US bombing campaigns are 'degrading their capacity to develop nuclear weapons and ultimately to deliver them.' The comments came the same weekend the US destroyed three Iranian oil tankers and Iran fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier group, underscoring that the administration sees military pressure — not diplomacy — as the near-term path on Iran, with implications for how long the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade and its oil-market disruption persist.
